remainingEvidence: The closure is enforced today and the enforcement predates the rule, so what is owed is conformance naming rather than behaviour. src/agents/runs/commit.ts declares a `run: RunId` field on RunCommit beside `branch`, and src/agents/runs/runtime.ts#RunRuntime rejects each of the three ways a foreign commit could enter one Run's graph: appendInTransaction rejects a branch whose `run` differs from the loaded Run with `Run commit target is invalid`, rejects a unary or first-merge parent whose `run` differs with `Run commit parent belongs to another Run`, and validateMerge cannot find a second-parent branch that this Run does not own because its source lookup filters on `branch.run.equals(target.run)`, so a foreign source head rejects with `Merge requires equal-pinned current heads from distinct branches`

Three p0 tests exercise exactly those three paths and none carries this atom's label, so no selector can be claimed until they are tagged. test/agents/runs/runtime-mutation.test.ts `append guards` > `rejects a parent commit that belongs to another Run` inserts a commit under RunId `run-elsewhere` and appends against it; `merge validation` > `merge requires an exact source branch and stored head commits` registers branch `branch-elsewhere` under RunId `run-elsewhere` and merges its head; `runtime lookup errors` > `effective commits reject a branch of another Run` covers the branch side. Moving this row to verified is the tagging plus ACQ-IMPORT and ACQ-TEST, not new behaviour

A positive assertion is owed alongside the rejections, because a runtime that rejected every merge would satisfy a rejection-only test: a merge whose source is a distinct branch of the same Run at equal pins is accepted, and the resulting graph still holds exactly one zero-parent commit. The second half is the interaction with C13-RUN-GRAPH-ARITY this rule depends on — closure and the single-root rule are one fact read from two directions — and no test asserts the zero-parent count after a merge

The whole-graph consequence a reader relies on has no check, only the three per-append checks that imply it. src/agents/runs/runtime.ts#RunRuntime spawnRunInTransaction creates the child Run with its own root commit, and nothing asserts that no commit of the parent Run is reachable from any commit of the child, nor that the child's graph holds exactly one zero-parent commit after arbitrary appends, merges, and branch creation. remainingEvidence: FacetSet has no representation in src. §4.1 now defines it as the canonical-ordered, unique FacetRef membership of one composition view, and §5.3 fixes a Turn's FacetSet to the facet refs of its immutable TurnPlacementSnapshot placements. Closure requires that derivation to exist once, over the existing TurnPlacementSnapshot record (src/agents/runs/placement.ts#TurnPlacementSnapshot), rather than as a second membership list a host could populate independently.

The no-second-composition-view conjunct has no enforcement point. src/agents/runs/executor.ts#validateOperations already rejects a TurnBoundOperation whose facet is absent from the immutable placement snapshot, which is membership stability for bound Operations only; nothing yet answers a general membership question from the captured set, and nothing prevents a host from answering one from the Scope's current install records instead. Closure requires the executor seam to expose the captured set as the Turn's only composition view.

The typed unavailability a withdrawn captured member yields at its next use has no error class and no reachable path, because withdrawal itself is planned: there is no retired-Binding state for a resolution attempt to observe, and C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-EXACT is a prerequisite for that reason.

The behavior test must prove both halves in one exercise over the public interface and must fail if either is traded for the other: an install and a withdrawal committed mid-Turn leave the Turn's membership identical, while a Grant revoked mid-Turn denies the next use of a member the Turn still composes. A test that asserts only stable membership would pass against a host that had frozen authority with it.

Every clause is downstream of C13-TURN-ADMISSION-HANDLE, which is itself planned: GatewayTurnInvocationPort returns Operation output only, so no handle is ever put in the model's tool position and there is nothing whose ownership could transfer. Until a handle exists the commit point cannot be exercised from either side, which is why this atom names that one as a prerequisite rather than restating it

The commit point needs both sides proved against the same admission: a Turn expired, cancelled, or lost before admission must yield a `cancelledPreEffect` Receipt with no EffectAttempt and no handle, while a Turn cancelled after admission must leave the item's Receipt to be appended against its frozen intent, placement, and Package pin. A test that only cancels before admission would pass against a host that revoked every handle on Turn cancellation

The prohibition is the clause a passing test hides. Cancelling the issuing Turn must not abort an item whose admission identity it published, so a mutation propagating the Turn's cancellation to a published handle must break a cited test rather than merely change timing; the discriminating observation is the failure kind, since such a host records `aborted` on an item this rule requires to settle on its own terms

The two owners must be shown distinct in one exercise, because a host that cascaded would pass every test that spawns and waits: cancelling the Run aborts an outstanding `InvocationId` handle and withholds Settled until that item has a terminal current Receipt, while cancelling a parent Run leaves a spawned child Run running and does not withhold the parent's Settled, the spawn's `delegate` Receipt already being terminal once it carries the child RunRef

Child-Run isolation needs an adversarial authority case rather than a timing one: a caller holding only the parent Turn's LeaseToken must fail to cancel the child Run under C13-TURN-EXACT-LEASE, and cancellation must succeed only through authority that reaches that child Run

The derived-ceiling exception needs its own case because it is the one thing that legitimately crosses the boundary: a child must exhaust an inherited `depth` or `wallClockMs` bound computed from the spawn lineage and a root RunCommit timestamp (C13-RUN-CEILING-REMAINDER) and cancel itself through its own §5.3 rows with the exhausted dimension recorded, rather than being cancelled by the ancestor that declared the ceiling
